title: SEC Probe Into Nvidia's Accounting Deepens Leadership Crisis
summary:
Reuters reported that US Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia, giving a focus to an inquiry first reported days earlier. It came the same week the chipmaker posted third-quarter revenue up **103%** year on year, its first results since Jensen Huang's resignation.

The story matters because doubt over the quality of earnings strikes at the heart of the AI trade, in which Nvidia's results have been the main proof of demand.
context:
- Strong numbers alone no longer reassure investors once governance is in question. Without its founder, Nvidia must now earn trust in its reporting as well as its growth.

- The probe follows Huang's exit over relationships including one with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy. California's attorney general has separately subpoenaed Nvidia over whether its chips reached China.

- The SEC under President Trump has pulled back on enforcement but says it will prioritise core fraud, including accounting violations. That makes an accounting-focused case against America's most valuable chipmaker especially notable.

title: Fed Minutes Flag AI Debt as Financial-Stability Risk and Point to More Hikes
summary:
Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting, released this week, showed that "almost all" officials now see further rate rises as likely appropriate, up from "most" in September. Policymakers also singled out the AI investment boom as a risk to both inflation and financial stability.

That matters because it marks a rare shift: the central bank is treating the AI buildout as a source of potential system-wide stress, not just a growth story, just as markets are pricing a December hike.
context:
- The Fed has turned back towards tightening after raising rates in September, then holding at **3.75%–4%** in October. Two officials dissented in favour of an immediate quarter-point rise.

- Staff warned that off-balance-sheet leasing and circular financing among AI firms could amplify losses if returns disappoint. Some officials worried supervisors may miss banks' indirect exposure via credit lines to private credit funds.

- Many participants also saw AI-driven demand for chips, power and construction as a material inflation risk. That undercuts the hope that AI's productivity gains would let the Fed ease sooner.

title: Anthropic Raises $81.3bn in the Biggest IPO on Record
summary:
Anthropic priced its Nasdaq listing at **$83** a share, above its initial $70–$78 range, raising about $81.3bn and overtaking SpaceX's June offering as the largest IPO ever. A further $26bn private placement was sold at the same price.

The deal matters as a test of how much public investors will pay for frontier AI developers. Its timing, in a week of heavy selling in AI stocks, shows how quickly that appetite can be tested.
context:
- Upsizing the deal and pricing above range signalled strong institutional demand going in. Fully diluted valuations at pricing were reported at roughly $1.4tn–$1.5tn, depending on the method used.

- Anthropic and SpaceX listing within months of each other mark the return of mega-IPOs after years of companies staying private. Together they test how much new equity supply public markets can absorb at once.

- The listing gives investors a pure-play AI model developer for the first time. Its share price will now act as a live gauge of sentiment towards AI spending, alongside chipmakers such as Nvidia.
